text:
Dallas is 9-5-2 with 20 points, and the most interesting thing about it is how little the offence has had to do with it. The Stars have scored 44 goals against 48.1 expected (expected goals measure the quality of chances), so the shooters are running a little cold. The goaltending has covered for them: 36 goals allowed on 44 expected, about eight saved above an average night. That gap is the season so far.

The line worth watching is Mikko Rantanen with Wyatt Johnston and Sam Steel. In 72 minutes at five on five they've taken 67% of the expected goals and allowed just 1.52 per hour. The old core of Roope Hintz and Jason Robertson has been shakier with Tyler Seguin (45%), better with Jamie Benn (65%). Robertson, for his part, scored three goals in 5:20 on Nov. 4, the third-fastest hat trick in franchise history, as NHL.com's Tom Gulitti noted. Benn was two points from 1,000 as of that night.

The worry is Miro Heiskanen, who left that game with an upper-body injury. Glen Gulutzan said, per Gulitti, "We're hoping right now that it's not as serious as we first thought." The penalty count (3.81 taken a game, 2.88 drawn) is the other leak. Our numbers still give Dallas an 82% playoff chance and a 99-point pace.
headline: The Stars are winning on goaltending and one new line
